reply_budget_proof.check: src/acp/grok.rs:37-40 requires value_bytes(params) <= 489472 before the question loop and before parse_form/responder publication.
reply_budget_proof.serializer: value_bytes and encode both use serde_json default compact serialization. value_bytes does not add a newline; encode adds one and rejects above FRAME. RequestId strings are valid_id: nonempty, <=256 bytes, no control characters. Worst escaped string id is 514 bytes including quotes.
reply_budget_proof.worst_case_static: Question text appears once in params and at most twice in the reply (answers key and annotations key). Previews and offered labels appear in params and at most once in the reply. Synthetic Other is the only selected label absent from params, 9 bytes per question. Notes content is re-encoded with the same serializer and is bounded by value_bytes(values) <= LOCAL_CONTENT. Uncovered envelope/id/map syntax for one minimal question and a max escaped id is 621 bytes; for 32 minimal questions it is 1334 bytes. Against minimum non-question wrapper slack, the tightest uncovered excess is 383 bytes, inside the 4096 reserve, leaving 3713 bytes even if notes consume the entire 65536 allowance. Escaping cancels because both sides count encoded bytes. A 600000-byte question alone exceeds 489472 and is rejected.
reply_budget_proof.not_executed: This margin was calculated from the frozen source and serde_json field order. This reviewer did not run the encoder.

checklist.title: Closed genuine Grok method/schema/modes; no fabricated prose/MCP questions.
checklist.evidence: src/acp.rs:2012-2031 dispatches only elicitation/create, _x.ai/ask_user_question, and session/request_permission. The unmatched arm returns method_not_found. grok::form accepts only mode default or plan (src/acp/grok.rs:19-21) and projects into the existing flat form schema. No prose or MCP decoder was added. Cargo.toml pins agent-client-protocol-schema =1.12.0 with default-features=false.

checklist.title: Exact session/tool/wire RPC identity and malformed scope rejection.
checklist.evidence: toolCallId must be a nonempty control-free id of at most 256 bytes before publication (src/acp/grok.rs:22-25, src/acp.rs:2694-2696). parse_form requires exactly one of sessionId or requestId, checks the live session, and rejects a foreign or malformed request scope (src/acp.rs:2131-2164). Inbound RPC ids are validated before incoming_request (src/acp.rs:1785-1787, 2632-2638). A Grok form error returns invalid_params on the original id (src/acp.rs:2024-2031) and does not publish an interaction.

checklist.title: Duplicate question/choice and question/option count bounds.
checklist.evidence: Question count must be 1..=FIELDS/2, and FIELDS is 64, so at most 32 (src/acp/grok.rs:33-35, src/acp.rs:35). Duplicate question text and duplicate option labels are rejected (src/acp/grok.rs:64-66 and 99-102). Each question is capped at OPTIONS and the running total, including a synthesized Other, is capped at OPTIONS=256 (src/acp/grok.rs:90-91 and 120-121, src/acp.rs:36). These checks happen before parse_form publication.

checklist.title: Nullable flags and scalar/multiselect semantics.
checklist.evidence: Omitted and null multiSelect/multi_select become single choice. A present non-null non-boolean is invalid-request. Both flag names together are rejected (src/acp/grok.rs:67-77). Single choice becomes type string/oneOf; multiple choice becomes type array/items.anyOf with minItems 1 (src/acp/grok.rs:128-131). The new budget predicate does not change this branching.

checklist.title: Original answers/previews/annotations/Other wire shape.
checklist.evidence: grok::response keys answers by the original question title and always emits a JSON array of selected labels (src/acp/grok.rs:168-176). Nonempty notes become annotations.notes. A preview is copied only when exactly one option is selected and that option carried a string preview (src/acp/grok.rs:177-194). Other is added only when the request did not already offer that label (src/acp/grok.rs:116-118). Cancel remains {outcome:cancelled} (src/acp/grok.rs:147 and src/acp.rs:168-172).

checklist.title: Shared scalar/array Other dependent-notes validation before capture and admission.
checklist.evidence: validate_form_values rejects Other, including any array element equal to Other, unless the grok_notes_key field is a nonempty string (src/acp.rs:2541-2557). Native values() calls that shared function before review/capture (src/tui/agent.rs:1648-1650 and 1668-1674). Broker admission calls it again before encode (src/acp.rs:874-877). Forms without grok_notes_key skip the predicate. The reply-budget predicate does not move or duplicate this rule.

checklist.title: Unsupported decline retains responder and is not offered natively.
checklist.evidence: Grok publication sets actions to accept/cancel only (src/acp.rs:2015-2017). Native F6 returns without sending when decline is absent (src/tui/agent.rs:1121-1124 and 1375-1380). An API decline reaches grok::response, which bails before encode (src/acp/grok.rs:148-150). That error is raised inside commit before selections are written, enqueue, selected state, or calls.insert (src/acp.rs:890-974). daemon acp_action returns the error without ending the target (src/daemon.rs:441-458). The pending responder stays pending.

checklist.title: Concrete worst-case reply bound: escaping, repeated keys, previews, max values/count/RPC.
checklist.evidence: See reply_budget_proof. The historical 600000-byte question is above the 489472 encoded-params limit, so the two 600000-byte keys cannot be published. For every request that passes the check, two encoded question keys, one copy of each request-owned preview, selected labels already present in params, a full LOCAL_CONTENT notes allowance, a 256-byte worst-escaped RPC id, null/number ids, 32 questions, and the newline fit in FRAME with at least 3713 bytes of static margin. This was not executed.

checklist.title: Ingress budget error on original RPC before canonical/native responder publication.
checklist.evidence: The predicate is inside grok::form before the schema loop (src/acp/grok.rs:37-40). incoming_request only calls parse_form after grok::form succeeds, and responders.insert for the interaction is after that success (src/acp.rs:2012-2081). The native regression asserts that original id and code and an empty interactions array (tests/acp/native/acceptance.rs:656-666).

checklist.title: First-valid canonical selection, stale losers and reused IDs/writer stamps.
checklist.evidence: pending_interaction still requires kind, pending state, and the responder mapping before an answer is encoded (src/acp.rs:1972-1990 and 872). Fallible validation and encode happen before enqueue, selected state, and calls.insert (src/acp.rs:890-974). A losing prepared action therefore cannot publish a second response. Responder write stamps still distinguish an unfinished write from a reused id (src/acp.rs:1984-1992 and 239-241). The new rejection never creates a selectable interaction, so it cannot become a second winner.

checklist.title: Atomic authority/generation-to-broker ordering and no late substitution.
checklist.evidence: daemon acp_action authorizes, prepares, then calls Authority::admit_acp, which holds the target lock, rechecks the live current control, and passes the captured generation into commit (src/daemon.rs:441-450, src/control.rs:1194-1208). commit rejects a changed generation and rechecks the exact target before mutation (src/acp.rs:752-762). The reply-budget failure is an inbound agent request, not an authority substitution. No late owner lookup was added.

checklist.evidence: The large fixture waits for the original-id -32602 response, writes grok-large-rejected.json, and returns bonus 0; the prompt then records effect 17+25+0 and emits end_turn (tests/fixtures/acp_peer.rs:748-766 and 860-875). checklist.title: Explicit interrupt plus applicable pending/late original-RPC responses.
checklist.evidence: Interrupt still requires the exact current foreground prompt, reserves session/cancel, and builds cancel frames for applicable pending interactions before commit (src/acp.rs:820-866). checklist.title: Exact offered permission allow/deny, no synthesized permission.
checklist.evidence: parse_permission still requires the live session, unique offered option ids, and only allow-once, allow-always, reject-once, or reject-always (src/acp.rs:2167-2198). Permission admission checks the submitted option_id against the offered list before encoding (src/acp.rs:910-918). The Grok codec does not synthesize a permission option or map decline/F6 to deny. The production delta does not touch this path.

checklist.title: Startup/close/shutdown races, ended authority and no resurrection.
checklist.evidence: Spawn is skipped when the target is already not live, and initialize publication goes through lifetime.with_live (src/acp.rs:1372-1428). close does not reopen a non-live target except to record a later process-identity or cleanup failure (src/acp.rs:383-390). Shutdown sets stopping and ends ACP views (src/daemon.rs:494-503). acp_action rejects input after stopping (src/daemon.rs:432-435). The budget error uses error_response and does not recreate an ended target.

checklist.title: Ingress/egress/call/retention budgets before irreversible publication.
checklist.evidence: read_frame rejects growth past FRAME before extension, and the reader reserves ingress count and QUEUE_BYTES before reading (src/acp.rs:1627-1655). Interaction publication calls retain_capacity before responders.insert (src/acp.rs:2079-2081). Answer commit encodes and checks writer/RPC capacity before enqueue and calls.insert (src/acp.rs:445-456 and 930-974). The new Grok predicate is an additional pre-publication bound, not a raised frame cap. A budget failure on an inbound question returns invalid_params instead of publishing an unanswerable interaction.

checklist.title: Lock order and no blocking I/O/spawn/join under admission locks.
checklist.evidence: Admission order remains target authority lock then broker state lock (src/control.rs:1194-1208, src/acp.rs:752-762). value_bytes is a CPU counter with no allocation of a second buffer and no I/O (src/acp.rs:2587-2598). Spawn, process termination, and worker joins remain outside those locks in run/cleanup (src/acp.rs:1348-1514 and 1115-1118). The new predicate does not acquire the authority lock or spawn.

checklist.title: Owned retained-pipe cleanup truth and joins, no capacity release on unknown.
checklist.evidence: cleanup_complete requires joined workers and refuses process-identity or cleanup failure (src/acp.rs:309-313). run terminates the birth-qualified tree, reaps, joins all pipe workers, checks endpoint hangup, and only then drops descriptors and calls finish (src/acp.rs:1468-1514). Failure sets lifecycle failed and failure cleanup before finish. The reply-budget path does not drop descriptors or release a charged unknown lifetime.

checklist.title: Birth-pinned owned process cleanup, unrelated sentinel preservation.
checklist.evidence: ProcessTree::capture_owned_session requires the child to be its own session leader (src/runtime.rs:716-718). If capture fails, the pinned child is reaped and the instance closes as process-identity without publishing a birth-qualified tree (src/acp.rs:1403-1409). The native finish helper reaps peer.pid, requires cleanup_complete, shuts the daemon down, asserts the private socket is gone, and checks the unrelated sentinel before removing the private root (tests/acp/native.rs:445-468, tests/acp.rs:420-425). The new test calls that same finish helper.
